events.title: The Greenhouse Problem
events.description: Food is running low and everyone is hungry. The Biologist is growing little potatoes with good bacteria (probiotics) in Mars-like soil. But the sprouts are still tiny! Do you eat them now, or wait?
events.nasa_fact: NASA's Curiosity rover tested soil in Gale Crater and found clay. Clay forms when there is water.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: do not eat the sprouts yet. Plants make your air and your future food.

options.label: Eat the sprouts now

delayed.text: With fewer plants, the air gets stuffy.

options.feedback: Yum! But the plants help make your air, and now the air feels stuffy.

options.label: Wait and share the food carefully

delayed.text: Harvest time! The plants are ready.

options.feedback: The Biologist protected the plants. They grow big and clean the air!
options.fail_feedback: Oh no! The little plants dried out. There will be no harvest this time.

options.label: Use extra power for the plant lights
options.feedback: The Engineer made the plants grow fast with bright lamps. It used a lot of battery!
options.fail_feedback: The lamps flickered and burned out. The battery is drained and the plants did not grow.

events.title: Space Tummy Ache
events.description: Space radiation is making the crew's tummies hurt. If you do not fix it today, tomorrow will be worse. Every day it keeps costing health.
events.nasa_fact: NASA scientists studied a tiny model of a human gut. A good bacteria called Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG helped protect it from space radiation.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: fix it today. Good bacteria help tummies stay strong in space.

options.label: Make shakes with good bacteria (probiotics)
options.feedback: Science to the rescue! The good bacteria protected everyone's tummies from the radiation.
options.fail_feedback: The shakes did not turn out right. Tummies still hurt.

options.label: Use the medicine box
options.feedback: The Doctor used medicine from the first-aid kit. Tummies feel better fast.
options.fail_feedback: That medicine was not the right kind. It did not help.

options.label: Wait until later
options.feedback: You wait. The crew feels a bit worse every morning.

events.title: The Space Blues
events.description: You have been staring at red rocks for many days. Being far from home can make people sad and forgetful. Everyone is grumpy and arguing.
events.nasa_fact: Scientists study tiny brain models grown in labs. They found that space travel can change how brains work.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: team activities help. People feel better together.

options.label: Hold a video game and music party
options.feedback: The Commander cheered everyone up. Laughs on Mars!
options.fail_feedback: The speakers broke and the party was a flop.

options.label: Play memory games and breathe calmly
options.feedback: The Doctor helped everyone relax and train their brains.
options.fail_feedback: Nobody could focus today. Maybe try again another day.

options.label: Ignore it and keep working

delayed.text: A tired crew member pressed the wrong button and bent a panel.

options.feedback: Everyone was distracted. Someone pressed the wrong button!

events.title: Rover in the Sand
events.description: Your little robot explorer is stuck in a sand dune and lost its signal. It has important science inside!
events.nasa_fact: In 2009, the Spirit rover got stuck in soft sand. NASA worked for months to free it.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: remember Spirit! Moving the wheels slowly, a little at a time, works best.

options.label: Drive it out by remote control
options.feedback: The Engineer wiggled the wheels from far away and freed it! It carried ice samples that give you air.
options.fail_feedback: The wheels spun and dug in deeper. The rover is still stuck.

options.label: Go outside in space suits to rescue it

chance.text: You also found a special rock: +10 Energy!

options.feedback: Awesome space walk! You freed the robot and collected rocks by hand.
options.fail_feedback: The sand was too soft. You came back tired, without the rover.

options.label: Leave the robot behind and save your stuff
options.feedback: The base is safe, but you lost a helpful explorer.

events.title: Dust on the Solar Panels
events.description: A dust storm covered the solar panels. They make less and less electricity. If you do nothing today, there will be even less light tomorrow.
events.nasa_fact: The Opportunity rover kept working for years because wind cleaned its solar panels. You cannot wait for the wind!
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: clean or reprogram the panels today. Waiting for the storm to pass costs a lot.

options.label: Go outside and wipe the panels
options.feedback: You swept off the dust by hand. It used air, but the panels shine again!
options.fail_feedback: The wind blew the dust right back. You used up air and still have no power.

options.label: Program the panels to shake off the dust

delayed.text: The panels shook off the dust: +15 Energy.

options.feedback: The Engineer made the panels wiggle. It uses battery today, but saves work tomorrow.
options.fail_feedback: There was a bug in the code. The panels did not wiggle.

options.label: Wait for the storm to pass
options.feedback: You rest today, but the storm drains your energy every morning.

events.title: A Calm Sol
events.description: No emergencies today. It is time to take care of the base. What will you do?
events.nasa_fact: Real space teams use quiet days for checkups and repairs.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: calm days are for getting ready.

options.label: Rest together
options.feedback: A good rest makes everyone happier.

options.label: Check the base walls
options.feedback: The Engineer tightened some loose seals.
options.fail_feedback: The Engineer found nothing to fix, but the checking still used energy.

options.label: Take care of the greenhouse
options.feedback: The Biologist cared for the plants. It smells like fresh soil and clean air.
options.fail_feedback: The Biologist watered too much. The plants did not get any better.

events.title: Build 3 Earthquake Sensors
events.description: To listen for Marsquakes, you need a network of 3 sensors. They break easily, so build them carefully before going outside.
events.nasa_fact: NASA's InSight lander heard more than 1,300 Marsquakes using a sensor called SEIS.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: build the sensors soon. A finished network gives you an early warning.

options.label: Print them with the 3D printer
options.feedback: The Engineer printed all three sensors. They work perfectly!
options.fail_feedback: The printer jammed! The sensors came out broken. You will have to try again.

options.label: Take parts from the old rover
options.feedback: You took the old rover apart. The sensors are ready, but the base lost some useful parts.
options.fail_feedback: The old parts did not fit. The sensors do not work.

options.label: Build them with duct tape and patience
options.feedback: It is not pretty, but duct tape fixes everything... for now.
options.fail_feedback: The tape came unstuck and the sensors fell apart.

events.title: Place the Sensors Outside
events.description: The 3 sensors are ready. Take them outside, spread them far from the base, and press them firmly into the ground. Air is precious out there!
events.nasa_fact: InSight placed its sensor right on the ground using a robot arm.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: use the precision tool. Less time outside means less air used.

options.label: One long walk outside
options.feedback: A long, tiring space walk, but all three sensors are listening!
options.fail_feedback: You got too tired and had to turn back. The sensors are still not planted.

options.label: Use the precision tool
options.feedback: The Engineer planted them perfectly. Less time outside means less air used.
options.fail_feedback: The tool slipped and the sensors were not planted well.

options.label: Two walks on two different Sols

delayed.text: Second walk done: all 3 sensors are in place!

options.feedback: You went out in two turns to catch your breath. Slower, but safer.
options.fail_feedback: The first walk went wrong. Try again tomorrow.

events.title: The Dusty Sensor
events.description: One sensor stopped sending data. Dust covers it, or a cable came loose. If you leave it, it does not count anymore.
events.nasa_fact: Dust was a big problem for InSight during its mission.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: try restarting the sensor from the base first. It saves air.

options.label: Go outside and fix it
options.feedback: You dug it out and it started sending data again!
options.fail_feedback: You could not reach the cable. The sensor is broken for good.

options.label: Restart it from the base
options.feedback: The Engineer restarted the signal from the base and the sensor woke up.
options.fail_feedback: The restart did not work. The sensor is lost.

options.label: Leave it
options.feedback: You left it behind. Now the network is missing a sensor.

events.title: Marsquake!
events.description: ALERT from the sensor network! A quake is about to hit the base. You have very little time to choose!
events.nasa_fact: InSight felt Marsquakes up to about magnitude 5. It used them to learn what is inside Mars.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: with an early warning, nobody has to get hurt.

options.label: Make the base walls stronger
options.feedback: Thanks to the warning, the Engineer strengthened the weak spots before the shaking.
options.fail_feedback: There was not enough time. A wall cracked during the quake.

options.label: Move everyone to the safe room
options.feedback: Everyone was safe when the quake arrived.
options.fail_feedback: Someone tripped in the dark. A few bumps and bruises!

events.title: Surprise Marsquake!
events.description: The ground shakes with no warning! The base creaks and some parts break. Without the full sensor network, there was no time to get ready.
events.nasa_fact: Without a network of sensors, nobody can know a quake is coming.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control cannot help right now: it is time to fix things.

options.label: Fix the damage
options.feedback: It took a lot of work, but the base is repaired.
options.fail_feedback: The repairs did not hold. More parts broke.

events.title: Build MOXIE: Part 1
events.description: Mars has almost no oxygen to breathe, but its air is full of carbon dioxide (CO₂). A machine called MOXIE can split CO₂ and make oxygen! Starting to build it uses a lot of energy.
events.nasa_fact: A machine called MOXIE rode on the Perseverance rover. It made oxygen from the air of Mars!
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: build it carefully. Energy is what you will miss most at the start.

options.label: Build it as fast as you can
options.feedback: You worked non-stop. The base was almost dark, but MOXIE is growing!
options.fail_feedback: You rushed and a part cracked. MOXIE is not ready yet.

options.label: Build it slowly and carefully
options.feedback: The Engineer used every tool wisely and saved energy.
options.fail_feedback: A tiny screw went missing. MOXIE is not ready yet.

options.label: Use parts from the greenhouse
options.feedback: It works, but the plants are not happy.
options.fail_feedback: The greenhouse parts did not fit. MOXIE is not ready yet.

events.title: MOXIE vs. the Greenhouse
events.description: MOXIE needs the same power as the plant lights. The Biologist worries that the plants will wilt if you cut their power. Share the electricity so nothing turns off!
events.nasa_fact: Sharing power between machines is a real problem on space missions.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: make a schedule. MOXIE at night, plants by day.

options.label: Give MOXIE all the power
options.feedback: MOXIE grows, but the plants are struggling.
options.fail_feedback: A fuse blew! MOXIE did not get its power.

options.label: Make a power schedule
options.feedback: The Biologist made a plan: MOXIE at night, plants by day. Everybody is happy!
options.fail_feedback: The schedule got mixed up and nothing got finished.

options.label: Turn off the lab and greenhouse for one Sol
options.feedback: A hard choice, but nobody argues with the Commander.
options.fail_feedback: Some machines would not restart after the blackout.

events.title: MOXIE: The Last Step
events.description: MOXIE's filter is clogged with Mars dust. If you do not fix it, the machine will break. You are one step away from finishing!
events.nasa_fact: MOXIE made about 12 grams of oxygen every hour.
events.earth_hint: Mission Control says: if you ignore the filter, you lose progress. Fix it!

options.label: Clean the filter by hand
options.feedback: It costs some air, but it works!
options.fail_feedback: The dust was stuck too hard. You will have to try again.

options.label: Swap in a new filter
options.feedback: A new filter, no surprises!
options.fail_feedback: The new filter was the wrong size.

options.label: Ignore it
options.feedback: The filter jammed completely. You must redo one part.

events.title: MOXIE Works!
events.description: The machine is at 100%! A beep tells you the first oxygen is coming from the air of Mars. From now on, the base does not lose air every day.
events.nasa_fact: 12 grams of oxygen per hour is about what an astronaut breathes in a few minutes.

options.label: We did it!
options.feedback: MOXIE is running! Air is not your problem anymore.

events.title: Solar Storm Alert!
events.description: NASA data shows a strong flare from the Sun. It blocks radio messages to Earth for 2 Sols. Protect the crew!
events.nasa_fact: NASA's DONKI system tracks solar flares and sun storms almost live.

options.label: Give the crew a probiotic boost
options.feedback: The Biologist made a boost of good bacteria to help everyone handle the radiation.
options.fail_feedback: The boost did not work. Everyone feels the radiation.

options.label: Turn on the base shields
options.feedback: The Engineer raised the shields. It uses energy, but the base is protected.
options.fail_feedback: The shields flickered. Some radiation got in.

options.label: Hide in the middle room
options.feedback: You spent hours squeezed in the middle room. Not comfy, but safe.
